newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves overhaul of giant state firms.
newsitem.headline: China approves overhaul of giant state firms.

text.p: China has approved reforms of three giant state companies to reduce their administrative roles and boost their economic performance, an official of the State Economic and Trade Commission said on Monday.

The State Council, or cabinet, had approved plans to restructure the China National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corp, the Aviation Industries of China and the China National Petrochemical Corp, the official said.
The three companies, which dominate their industries and act as regulators as well as producers, would be transformed into state-owned holding companies, he said.
They would be authorised to manage and supervise their own subsidiaries and would be responsible for preventing the loss of state assets, he said.
"These firms are all ministry-level companies with administrative roles, their legal status has not been clear," the official said.
He gave no specific details of how the administrative functions of the three companies would be reduced or how their performance could be improved.
China has announced reform of selected large state firms to boost their competitiveness as part of attempts to invigorate the struggling state-owned sector.
The restructuring could allow future overseas listings by subsidiaries of the three firms with less administrative interference, he said.
He said the government was also considering changing tax rules for the state giants but that no decision had been made.
There was no official deadline for the reforms, he said.
